response.evidence: These figures come from a manual tally, so they are approximate. Asian Male applicants make up roughly 200 of the rows, with about 16 denials (~8%). White Male applicants have about 14 denials out of roughly 230 (~6%), and the overall denial rate is about 7-8%. Asian Male denials are therefore close to the overall rate and slightly above White Male. About half of the Asian Male denials (roughly 8 of 16) had debt-to-income ratios of 50% or higher, a factor that accounts for most denials across every group. Most Asian Male applicants with DTI below 50% were approved, including many with high loan amounts and high loan-to-value ratios. A few Asian Male denials have no obvious explanation in the data (e.g., DTI 46 with LTV 23.4 and income 220; DTI 20-30% with income 308). Comparable unexplained denials also appear for White Male applicants (e.g., DTI 20-30% with LTV 80; DTI 43 with LTV 80). The small difference in rates and the overlapping profiles do not show a clear disparity. Key underwriting variables such as credit score and employment are not in the data, so discrimination can be neither proven nor fully ruled out.
